manifests.name: a stateless profile of one rego partition
manifests.yaml:
metadata:
  kind: policy
  name: vectors
runtimes:
  rego:
    language: { name: rego, constraint: ">=1.0.0" }
    engine:   { name: permguard, constraint: ">=0.1.0 <0.2.0" }
partitions:
  rules:
    runtime: rego
    schema: false
profiles:
  default: { type: permguard.api.pdp.native.v1, partitions: [rules] }

manifests.name: a language range this build does not meet
manifests.yaml:
metadata:
  kind: policy
  name: vectors
runtimes:
  rego:
    language: { name: rego, constraint: ">=99.0.0" }
    engine:   { name: permguard, constraint: ">=0.1.0 <0.2.0" }
partitions:
  rules:
    runtime: rego
profiles:
  default: { type: permguard.api.pdp.native.v1, partitions: [rules] }

expect.refused: manifest rejected: runtime `rego`: language rego 1.0.0 does not satisfy `>=99.0.0`

manifests.name: a temporal profile naming a rego partition
manifests.yaml:
metadata:
  kind: policy
  name: vectors
runtimes:
  rego:
    language: { name: rego, constraint: ">=1.0.0" }
    engine:   { name: permguard, constraint: ">=0.1.0 <0.2.0" }
partitions:
  rules:
    runtime: rego
profiles:
  default: { type: permguard.api.pdp.temporal.v1alpha1, partitions: [rules] }

expect.refused: manifest rejected: the profile `default` is `permguard.api.pdp.temporal.v1alpha1` and names the partition `rules`, which runs `rego` — a runtime that decides from the request alone. A temporal profile records history and decides against it, and there is no conversion that would make a stateless partition do so
